aspects.says: Since JDK 18 Method.invoke calls through a method handle, and the JIT inlines it only when the Method is a constant: a static final field or a record component reached through one, not a final field of an ordinary class.
basis: section:Since JDK 18, Method.invoke Is Fast Only When the JIT Sees a Constant

aspects.says: A method handle in a static final field costs what a direct call costs; in a plain field it is several times slower, yet still faster than a Method in a field.
basis: section:A Method Handle Obeys the Same Rule, and invokeExact Never Boxes
aspects.reason: a timing that depends on the JIT and the machine, which no deterministic test can grade; the quiz's question on a constant Method checks the same rule

aspects.says: Method.invoke boxes each int argument and result outside the Integer cache, and escape analysis removes only the argument array; a handle bound to its receiver and called with invokeExact allocates nothing.
basis: section:A Method Handle Obeys the Same Rule, and invokeExact Never Boxes

aspects.says: Looking a method up costs several times the call and returns a new Method each time, so a cache keyed by class, name and parameter types looks each method up once and stores it already accessible.
basis: section:Looking a Method Up Costs More Than Calling It, So Look Up Once

aspects.says: On JDK 21 -Djdk.reflect.useDirectMethodHandle=false brings back the pre-JDK 18 implementation, which beats the new one only while a single Method passes through the call site; JDK 25 ignores the flag.
basis: section:The Pre-JDK 18 Reflection Won Only While One Method Used the Call Site

aspects.says: setAccessible(true) skips the access check inside invoke and saves under a nanosecond; repeating it before every call costs nothing measurable, so the lookup, not the flag, is what to cache for speed.
basis: section:Looking a Method Up Costs More Than Calling It, So Look Up Once

aspects.says: A timed loop whose results are never used can be deleted by the JIT and measures nothing; a harness warms up, uses every result and compares in fresh JVMs.
basis: section:A Loop Whose Result Nobody Reads Measures Nothing
